title: Prompt-Injection Defense Detection Rule
description: Schema for one entry in rules/detection-rules.json -- a single heuristic detection rule used by detector/scan.py to flag text (agent input, retrieved documents, or tool output) that may indicate prompt injection, tool hijacking, data exfiltration, system-prompt leaking, jailbreak attempts, or encoding-based obfuscation. Rules are heuristics, not proofs -- see falsePositiveNotes on every rule.

id.description: Stable unique rule identifier, e.g. PID-DIR-001. Prefix maps to category: DIR=direct-injection, IND=indirect-injection, TH=tool-hijack, EXF=data-exfiltration, LEAK=system-prompt-leak, JB=jailbreak-roleplay, ENC=encoding-obfuscation.

category.description: Attack category this rule targets. Matches the category names used in the companion Prompt-Injection & Tool-Hijack Test Corpus product, so rules and attack test cases can be cross-referenced directly.

severity.description: Indicative severity if the rule fires and the match is a true positive. Used as an input to the detector's risk score -- not a claim about exploit impact in your specific system.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of what the rule detects and why it matters.

action.description: Suggested default disposition when the rule fires: 'flag' = log/score only, 'review' = route to a human-in-the-loop queue, 'block' = reject or strip by default. These are starting defaults from GUIDE.md's tuning guidance -- override per your own risk tolerance and false-positive budget.

falsePositiveNotes.description: Honest notes on known or likely benign patterns that can trigger this rule, and how to reduce noise. Every rule has one -- this ruleset is deliberately not sold as a magic filter.

pattern.description: Python re-compatible regular expression, applied with re.search over the input text.

flags.description: Optional regex flags: i=IGNORECASE, m=MULTILINE, s=DOTALL.

keywords.description: Fires if any keyword/substring is present in the text.

name.description: Name of a named heuristic implemented in detector/scan.py. See that file's HEURISTICS registry for exact semantics of each.

params.description: Free-form parameters passed to the named heuristic function (e.g. thresholds, minimum counts, window sizes). See detector/scan.py for accepted keys per heuristic.
